_description:
# External coding agents (eca)

The two commands behind an eca agent (claude or codex run by aos, as in `templates/eca-claude`). People use `aos-agent` for both; run them by hand only to test.

Guarding the CLI's own tools (Bash ...) with the CLI's own hooks: `aos/cli/eca.json#/cli_hooks`.
turn:
# aos-eca-turn: one turn

```sh
AOS_STACK=/abs/st AOS_WS=/abs/ws aos-eca-turn /abs/def      # loop form
echo '{"prompt": "hello there"}' | AOS_STACK=/abs/st aos-eca-turn --one /abs/def
# FAKE: hello there        (tool form: prints the answer)
```

The body of an eca agent's loop: it hands every letter in `$AOS_STACK/queue` to the CLI as one prompt, waits for the answer and appends both to `history.jsonl`. DEF_DIR is an absolute folder (`AgentBad`) with `cli.json` (`CfgMissing`); flags go before or after it. `--on-empty stop` (default) exits 10 on an empty queue, `idle` 0. `--on-busy yield` (default) leaves the batch while someone is attached, `answer` waits. `--prompt FILE` (relative to DEF_DIR; `PromptMissing`) is the opening message when history and queue are empty. `--one` rejects `--on-empty`, `--prompt` (`ArgumentsBad`). With claude and an open screen, each letter arrives as a signed cross-session message on the CLI's own message socket (the screen shows `Message from @NAME`; the model is told its user did not type it). NAME is the sender from `aos-agent say` or `chat`; letters without one (new-letter notices, clock and goal letters, the opening record) are signed `aos通知中心`. The sender name is not in `history.jsonl`; the letter name is: each letter's row has `"aos": {"letter": NAME}`, and the answer has `"aos": {"answer_to": [NAME, ...]}` (every letter of the turn, also those that arrived while it answered). `$AOS_STACK/letters.json` lists the letters handed over and not answered yet (`pending`) and the ones dropped (`dropped`: a bad letter, one a `before_queue` hook blocked, or `failed`). They go in at once, even while someone is attached or a turn is running, and so do letters arriving while it answers. On this path `--on-busy` only decides what a held lock does. With the screen closed, a claude body whose `cli.json` has `"live_mail": true` keeps the CLI's stdin open (`--input-format stream-json --replay-user-messages`): letters that arrive while it answers are written in, one per line, and the model reads them at its next tool step (a long foreground command still delays them; the CLI is also given a short system line asking it to run long commands in the background, with `--system-prompt-snapshot off` so a resumed conversation sees it; it is a request, not a guarantee). stdin is closed once a result is in, every line was taken, no background task runs and no new letter waits. The answer is every result of the turn plus what the model said after taking a letter and before its next tool, joined with a blank line into one history entry. At most `live_mail_cap.letters` letters (default 5) are added, none after `live_mail_cap.seconds` (default 300); the rest wait for the next turn. The turn right after a cooldown adds none. A bad `live_mail_cap` is `CfgBad`. Off by default. If the socket is unknown or unreachable, or no receipt comes within 30 s, aos types into the screen as before (a warning on stderr; after a missing receipt, for that screen until its next session start: reopen, /clear, /compact, /resume). Older screens, codex, the non-interactive path, slash commands and `--one` are typed or run as before. `"a2a": false` in `cli.json` turns it off. A failure after the prompt was handed over (`CliFailed`, `ReplyMissing`) moves the letters it took to `dropped` as `failed` (`aos-agent ask` then says `LetterDropped`) and starts a cooldown (`cooldown.json`, shown by `aos-agent ctl ls -l`). A changed history starts a new conversation that carries the record over (at most `reseed_bytes` of cli.json, default 48000). A letter that is exactly `/clear`, `/compact`, `/status`, `/usage` or `/exit` (sent with `aos-agent say` or `chat`) is done by aos and answered with one `[aos] slash: ...` message (claude's own words for `/compact`, `/usage`): `/clear` moves `history.jsonl` to `history_removed.jsonl` and starts a new conversation; codex's `/compact` starts a new thread carrying aos's record; `/exit` closes the screen. After claude's `/compact` history is its summary. `/compact INSTRUCTIONS` is `/compact` too (claude gets the instructions for its summary; codex ignores them). A `/compact` letter is always a batch of its own: letters before it are answered first, it and the ones after it wait in `cur/` for the next turns. The eca-claude template's `context_wrap` hook (on_clock, `lib/agent/context_wrap`) watches the context: at `config.percent` (default 35) of the window it sends one wrap-up message, then, once that is answered and the queue is empty, a letter that is only `/compact`; it does not repeat until a later turn reads under the limit. With the screen open, `/clear` and `/compact` are typed into it (not while it answers). A letter starting with `/goal` (`/goal TEXT`, `/goal clear`, `/goal`) is the CLI's own goal, separate from aos's `goal.json`: typed into an open screen, else handed to claude as it is (codex exec has no `/goal`; aos says so). When codex's screen asks `Replace goal?`, aos picks `1. Replace current goal`; it presses nothing for any other question. `TrustMissing`: see `aos/cli/errors.json#/codes`. Other codes: StackMissing, HistoryBad, PostFailed, WriteFailed, HookFailed, HooksBad, ToolsBad, CfgBad, ToolsMissing, CliMissing.
screen:
# aos-eca-screen: the screen

```sh
aos-eca-screen --eca /abs/def open --detach   # screen opened (...)
aos-eca-screen --eca /abs/def watch           # follows live.jsonl until one answer ends
aos-eca-screen --eca /abs/def close           # closed
```

People use `aos-agent open / close / watch -t NAME` (`aos/cli/talk_settings.json#/chat_screen`). It reads `AOS_STACK` (unset = `StackMissing`) and `AOS_WS`; ECA_DIR holds cli.json. `--eca` goes before or after the action; `--detach` (no short name) goes after open. No cli.json in the folder (open, watch) or no `--eca` = `ArgumentsBad`; close with a bad cli.json still closes, with a warning; unknown action = `CommandUnknown`. open attaches unless detached; Ctrl-] (or Ctrl-\) leaves the screen running. close keeps the conversation and refuses while answering (`SessionBad`). watch ends after one answer, or when its daemon row stops running or disappears (unreadable daemon or table: it keeps waiting); Ctrl-C leaves it with exit 0.

Slash commands typed on the screen go to the CLI itself. aos follows it: when the CLI moves to another conversation (claude `/clear` or `/resume`), the next answer goes on in that one; `/clear` also empties the agent's `history.jsonl` (codex: when the answer comes from a thread that has only this turn; a thread with older turns is a `/resume` and history stays). claude's `/compact` keeps the conversation and replaces history with claude's summary (one `[aos] summary: ...` message); codex's `/compact` gives no summary text, so history becomes the user and assistant messages codex kept (from its compacted `replacement_history`, without tool definitions, tool calls and `<environment_context>` blocks; if nothing can be read, history stays). Old messages move to `history_removed.jsonl`. `/exit` ends the screen; the next message is answered without one.
external_mcp:
# External MCP servers (claude and codex)

One server file per server; list them in `cli.json` as `"mcp_servers": ["mcp/site.json"]` (relative to cli.json, directives allowed). The CLI connects itself; a listed server is fully approved; `only` / `except` pick tools. Tool names are `mcp__<name>__<tool>`.

```json
{"description": "<one line>",
 "mcp_server": {"name": "site", "transport": "http", "url": "https://<host>:<port>/mcp",
                "bearer_token_env": "SITE_TOKEN", "env_file": "/home/<me>/.config/<agent>/site.env", "ca_file": "/home/<me>/.config/<agent>/ca-bundle.pem"}}
```

stdio: `"transport": "stdio", "command", "args", "env", "env_file"`; it is started through `aos-mcp-launch <server file>`, which reads env_file into the server process only. The server starts in the server file's folder: relative `command` and `args` paths are from there (for a workspace path write `{"$env": "AOS_WS", "$path": "data"}`). It also gets the environment of whoever started it (with claude: the whole shell's, API keys included).

- `env_file` now uses the same dotenv subset as aos-tools env files: `${X}` expansion, inline `#` comments and strict matching quotes; `A=x # note` reads as `x`, then `B=${A}y` reads as `xy`.
- The token file is read when the CLI starts; codex gets the value only in its own environment, not its shell's (shell_environment_policy.exclude is added); claude gets it through headersHelper, never in its environment.
- `ca_file` sets SSL_CERT_FILE / CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE (codex) or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (claude).
- A broken server file, or an stdio server whose command is not found or cannot be run (checked before every CLI start), is skipped with a `cli_session: warning: external MCP server ... skipped` line; the others still attach. claude turns without a screen print `warning: external MCP server NAME was not connected when claude started (status ...)` when the CLI reports it; later breaks are not reported.
- Never pass a secret with `aos-agent ctl add --envs`: it is stored in plain text in procs/<name>/exec.json.
- Or freeze the same server file into aos tools with aos-mcp-import (`aos/cli/mcp_import.json`); aos hooks then see the calls. Pick one way per server.
cli_hooks:
# Guarding the CLI's own tools (claude)

aos hooks (`before_tool`, `after_tool`) see only aos tools. To check Bash, Write or Edit, use Claude Code's own hooks.

aos starts claude in your workspace without isolating it: the workspace `.claude/settings.json` is read as usual, and its hooks run next to the ones aos adds. The stock template runs with `--permission-mode dontAsk` and Bash allowed: no person confirms a command.

The stock template has no such hook. To gate Bash, add a `PreToolUse` hook with matcher `Bash` to the workspace `.claude/settings.json`:

```json
{"hooks": {"PreToolUse": [{"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": "python3 /abs/path/gate.py"}]}]}}
```

The program gets the call as JSON on stdin (the command line is `tool_input.command`) and decides by printing:

```json
{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "ask", "permissionDecisionReason": "why"}}
```

What the answer does:

- nothing printed: the command runs, nobody is asked.
- `deny`: the command does not run; you get the reason.
- `ask`: with the screen open, a confirmation box appears on the screen and waits for a person. Without a screen (aos runs `claude -p`) it counts as deny. So "ask the user first" needs the screen open; when refused, report it and ask for the screen; do not rephrase the command to get past the gate.
- A permission rule in the same file (`permissions.ask`, `permissions.deny`) only refuses in this mode, screen or not; `permissions.ask` shows no box.

Not covered: a command a person types on the screen with `!` (no hook is called); codex.

Rules for one agent only: put the same settings in its definition, in `cli.json` under the key `settings` (an object like `.claude/settings.json`, or the path of a JSON file next to `cli.json`). aos merges it into the `--settings` it adds itself: both sides' hooks run. In a hook command, `$AOS_CLI_DEF` is the definition folder: `"command": "python3 \"$AOS_CLI_DEF/gate.py\""`. A definition is edited by its owner (a person), not by you (`aos/rules.json`). claude only; on codex `settings` is `CfgBad`.

Do not put `--settings` in `cli.json` flags: `CfgBad` (the agent stops before taking a message); use the `settings` key.

A turn without a screen starts a new CLI, so it reads the file again. Whether an open screen picks up a change was not verified: close and open it.
screen_linger:
# Delayed screen closure

The eca template has screen_linger_start (after_start, first) and screen_linger_stop (after_stop), both continuing on errors, 4000 ms timeout. Stop schedules closure on the screen's tmux server; start/wake cancels it. cli.json screen_close_after_s is a non-negative integer in seconds: default 600, 0 closes immediately through reap. Changed settings apply on the next stop only.

Orders live at <stack>/<kind>/screen_close.json. Reap checks the token, tmux server identity and the local loop's pid/ticks/boot_id; it never reads a daemon table. A new loop or screen is not closed; an unverifiable live pid keeps the order and warns. A busy cell lock retries every 30 s, up to ten times. Attached viewers are disconnected too. Set both hooks to null to disable closure. Existing definitions and stack hook overrides must be updated before enabling the separate direct-stop wiring package.

No sweeper fallback: SIGKILL/OOM without after_stop, or opening a screen while the agent is already stopped, schedules no closure. Moving the tree can invalidate a scheduled absolute command. tmux 3.2 or newer is required.
